notes.title: It tears the soul apart piece by piece
notes.notes:
In the dark universe of The Medium, The Maw stands out as a terrifying entity born from human trauma and suffering. It is an adversary whose presence haunts the player like a shadow. As a metaphor for destructive pain, it tears the soul apart piece by piece. 

[previewyoutube=tzOBdVFSbQE;full][/previewyoutube]

The Maw’s appearance evokes nightmarish visions. Its humanoid silhouette, with grotesquely elongated limbs and a disfigured face, triggers a primal fear. The creature’s voice, masterfully brought to life by Troy Baker, is equally unsettling—full of strange whispers and promises of destruction. The Maw speaks, revealing its twisted desire to consume its victims in an attempt to drown out its own suffering. 

Narratively, The Maw is tied to the past of the protagonist, Marianne, and the dark history of the Niwa Resort. It symbolizes how unresolved tragedies can sometimes fester into something genuinely dangerous. 

The game introduces elements of stealth and survival in dealing with The Maw. Playing as Marianne, the player has no means of fighting the monster directly—instead, they must avoid confrontation, hide in the shadows, and rely on the protagonist’s unique psychic abilities to survive. 

The Maw is a terrifying nightmare that not only haunts the protagonist but also plants a lingering unease within the player, a reminder that the worst demons are born in the human mind. It is a being that leaves an indelible mark, long after the game has ended. 

Also be sure to  check a pulse-pounding, third-person survival horror with a gripping and twisted time travel story!

The game is coming to PC (Steam) and consoles in 2025!

notes.title: Between Suffering and Redemption
notes.notes:
Marianne is a medium, capable of communicating with spirits and moving between the material and spiritual worlds. This extraordinary ability makes her both the driving force of the story and a tragic figure, struggling with her own traumas as she discovers dark truths about herself. Marianne’s appearance in the Spirit World differs from her real-world self. With her white hair and the bright light of her powers, she resembles a candle in the darkness, guiding lost souls through the void. 

  [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/a4156f766e7e44c9600aa65c316e6092a75268ca.jpg[/img]

The inspiration for Marianne’s role as a guide came from the mysterious [b]lanterns of the dead[/b], widely known as [i][b]lanternes des morts[/b][/i]. Between the 12th and 14th centuries, these lanterns were erected in many places across Europe. Through their light, they pointed the way for people lost in the darkness and announced the proximity of sacred places—locations caught between the earth and the heavens. These lanterns acted as waypoints for both the living and the dead. They also dispelled the gloom, where penitent souls or wraiths might have hidden— and revealed criminals lurking to prey on travelers. The dual purpose of the lanterns of the dead has fascinated historians for centuries. 

  
[b]Fun Fact: [/b]

[i]Most surviving [i]lanternes des morts[/i] are located in France, particularly in the Limousin region. They can also be found in Poitou and Berry, with a few examples in Spain and Great Britain. [/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/b59df9c7f49e83e0cb7f594f42ab00ff0c1babac.jpg[/img]
  
At first glance, Marianne’s abilities seem to be useful tools for helping spirits trapped in the spiritual world. However, the game quickly makes it clear that her gift is also a curse. Marianne doesn’t just see the suffering of others—she relives her own pain repeatedly. The truth about her past raises questions about her mission. We leave the answers to you - look for them by delving into our story about a true medium - a living [b][i]lanternes des morts[/i][/b]. 

Also be sure to  check a pulse-pounding, third-person survival horror with a gripping and twisted time travel story!

The game is coming to PC (Steam) and consoles in 2025!

notes.title: Polish themes in The Medium
notes.notes:
[h3]Hey The Medium community![/h3]

This week [i]The Medium[/i] takes part in the special [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/frompolandwithlove2024]Poland-themed Steam event[/url] together with other games by our talented friends from our country. 

To celebrate this, we’ve prepared a discount for our game so be sure to check it if you still wish to experience the mysterious story of Marianne. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1293160/The_Medium/ 

Meanwhile, for this occasion, we also have a number of facts about the game that are related to the country where it was developed.

Check out the the list of Polish themes in [i]The Medium[/i]! 

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Story Setting[/b][/h3]

The story of The Medium is set in Kraków, Poland, and the locations featured in the game are real. Marianne resides in a tenement in the Old Town, which is also the same building where the events of Observer: System Redux occur.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/e25dd1d81743daa71ab39a93cf3509c23871b300.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]King's Monument[/b][/h3]

Next to the tenement, there is a monument of the Polish king, Władysław II Jagiełło, which was revealed in 1910. It commemorates the 500th anniversary of the Battle of Grundwald (1410), where the king defeated the German Teutonic Order. The monument is visible in the intro video of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/974d25d7362c8684b71be21f2721b9c8326dbff0.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Marrianne's flat[/b][/h3]

The flat where Marianne and Jack live is filled with iconic interior decorations and references to Polish culture from the 90s, such as furniture, carpets, pictures, and potted plants.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/1052ba742475b39364ea561ecd888e3600e65faf.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Classic coffee/tea cups[/b][/h3]

The metal holder for a coffee glass that Marianne uses in the beginning scenes of the game is an iconic one, used in Polish homes for decades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/637ac05ef7ae18cfa5f6c12d152747b3e61fce0d.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]The Black Madonna of Częstochowa[/b][/h3]

In Jack's room and office, you can see a picture called "The Black Madonna" It is a reproduction of the painting located in The Jasna Góra Monastery in Poland, which was a very popular depiction of Saint Mary.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/39bd732e9c2af80adf8074ae7ac8db35855e39d0.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]FCS "ŻUK"[/b][/h3]

FSC "Żuk," the van parked in the courtyard of the tenement, was one of the most popular and iconic delivery vehicles in the history of Poland.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/9caefebcc5800dcb74329756048bc8da7d07c224.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]

[h3][b]Fiat 126p ("Maluch")[/b][/h3]

It is said that the Polish Fiat 126p "Maluch" ("the little one") was the cornerstone of automobile transport in Poland. Two wreckages of this vehicle can be seen next to the Niwa Resort entrance. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/7a81adeb600c16ac1322fcac3bc1015e4a4e1ca1.jpg[/img]


See you in the next one!

notes.title: Unveiling the Real World Inspiration For Our Game
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/ca84163f4ab3f6d425500cf6607255650bbee56a.jpg[/img]

A Haunting Homage: Did you know the abandoned Niwa holiday resort in the game is based on a real location in Krakow? You can even visit it yourself! But Niwa isn't the only slice of reality depicted in The Medium. Marianne's tenement house and the square outside are also meticulously recreated. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/dd2955a0253f3e1cb37a0a0f5ab0458fb8dbcf73.jpg[/img]
 

Stepping into the Real Niwa: The mosaic adorning the resort's hall is a faithful replica, as is the entire hall itself. While the in-game hotel rooms capture the essence of the real Niwa, they are by necessity condensed for gameplay purposes. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/5203681598cc65ea73094c444cdd88ee72f592e5.jpg[/img]

A Tribute to Beksiński: The Spirit World wouldn't exist without the profound influence of the brilliant Zdzisław Beksiński. Several elements pay homage to him, such as the imposing Eagle in Thomas's office. 

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/ab1b955edaa95f3629517dffa010497f4bfeba54.jpg[/img]

Marianne - A Beacon of Hope: In the bleakness of The Spirit World, Marianne shines like a candle in the dark. Her white hair, pale skin, and subtle ethereal glow all contribute to this symbolism. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/b59df9c7f49e83e0cb7f594f42ab00ff0c1babac.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Layers Of Fear dev's next original game will be revealed this year
notes.notes:
Twitter user pl_evil has helpfully translated a recent letter to shareholders from Bloober Team, showing that their new game "Project C" will be revealed later this year. This will be the studio's next original game, after they wrapped up Layers Of Fear last year with, confusingly, Layers Of Fear (the natural progression for a series: Layers Of Fear, Layers Of Fear 2, and then Layers Of Fear again, although it was going to be called Layers Of Fears at one point).

Bloober Team are currently doing a lot of IP work for other people, with the Silent Hill 2 remake due out later this year, and a game codenamed "Project R" in concert with Skybound Entertainment. Skybound are The Walking Dead company, so I wouldn't give you long odds for a bet on what Project R is about. Neither would I be surprised if Project C is unveiled this summer by a man named Geoff with shiny shiny trainers. I'm interested to see what it is, and honestly I'm hoping it's a brand new standalone thing, rather than a forced sequel to Observer or 2021's The Medium (where I got the header).

notes.title: The Medium is more Polish than most Polish-made games
notes.notes:
Poland is a well-represented country when it comes to game development. From CD Projekt Red's bombastically ambitious RPGs to Techland's Dying Light, to wonderful indie games like Frostpunk, Book of Demons, and Farm 51's horror games like Get Even and Painkiller: Hell & Damnation, the Polish dev scene isn't lacking. But amid all these Polish-made games, few have actually depicted Poland itself. The Medium breaks this unfortunate tradition beautifully, using the apartment at the start of the game to take a surprisingly close look at the country in which it was made.

In fact, right from the opening cutscene, which floats through Krakow's Plac Matejki before zooming into Jack's apartment, it's clear that developer Bloober Team desperately wants to use worldbuilding to introduce us to a culture that's been behind so many games yet rarely depicted itself.

Jack's apartment is in a beautiful but poorly maintained building, built around the turn of the 20th century. Look out the window, and through the fog you'll see the nebulous outlines of a monument harking back to arguably Poland's most illustrious time in history: the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth's victory over the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410.

notes.title: The Medium pushes PC hard - and even 1080p60 is off the table for high-end rigs
notes.notes:
After spending some time with The Medium on Xbox Series consoles, we were eager to try out the game on PC. It's an impressive title that at once pays homage to the survival horror titles of years gone by, while at the same time delivering some impressive - and technologically ambitious - new features. Bloober's dual viewport rendering concept clearly presents a huge challenge to the graphics capabilities of Microsoft's next-gen consoles, with even the mighty Series X employing dynamic resolution scaling that could see the title dip beneath a native 1080p - so how does the PC version deal with this and what are the extra features delivered to those with more powerful hardware? And to address the point raised by many PC users who've played the game - is it really 'unoptimised'? And if performance is poor, can Nvidia's remarkable DLSS AI upscaling technology turn it around?

In point of fact, Bloober employs both DXR-based hardware-accelerated ray tracing in The Medium and Nvidia DLSS comes along for the ride, principally in off-setting the additional cost in utilising RT features. But DLSS also improves upon native resolution image quality. In fact, in scenes we tested comparing Xbox Series X running at a higher native pixel-count to DLSS on PC, Nvidia's AI upscaling managed to deliver palpably cleaner results. As an interesting side-not, The Medium is based on Unreal Engine 4, and so therefore it's using its own temporal-based upscaling solution. It's one of the best around, but DLSS is still delivering a significantly improved image, even in its performance mode, where a 4K image is reconstructed from native 1080p resolution.

After image quality, there's the implementation of RT reflections, where Xbox renders these at a quarter of the current native resolution (remember that The Medium uses dynamic resolution scaling, with a very wide 900p to 2160p range). If there's one criticism I have of the RT features on PC, it's that there's very little granularity in the settings - so reflections always render out at full resolution: a hefty 4x increase in resolution. Bloober also uses a console-specific form of RT reflections by biasing reflections to be more mirror-like, making them cheaper to render. This feature can be enabled on PC, it is a part of UE4, but you'll need to use Unreal Engine Console Unlocker to access it. These are features available, easily tweakable, but I feel that the graphics menu option should open up these settings to the end user.

notes.title: The Medium review - non-violent hill
notes.notes:
A haunted Soviet workers' resort deep in the forests of Kraków. A protagonist who can not only talk with the dead, but literally walk through their world. And a ten foot-tall demon that wants to wear your skin (and won't shut up about it). The Medium is very spooky.

But it's not just about scary things, it's about how developer Bloober Team introduces and handles them. Comparisons to Silent Hill have followed the Polish studio since its debut, Layers of Fear, and they're even harder to shake in The Medium. The abandoned holiday complex Niwa isn't shrouded in fog, but Bloober Team's approach to horror is led by atmosphere, tension, and an unsettling soundtrack. Oh, and fixed camera angles.

You play as Marianne, a mortician who's haunted by visions of a dead girl by a lake. Early into the game you receive a phone call inviting you to Niwa from someone who claims to understand your visions. The resort itself is peak Soviet desolation porn: a brutalist block of concrete and faded grandeur. As you enter the lobby you encounter a ghost called Sadness, causing Marianne to enter an undead world that's heavily inspired by the surrealist art of Polish painter Zdzisław Beksiński.

notes.title: The Medium has been refused classification in Australia
notes.notes:
[img]https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8GT8v4wGMovyUxaYyRYBwm.jpg[/img]

[img]https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8GT8v4wGMovyUxaYyRYBwm.jpg[/img]

The Medium is the next psychological horror game from Bloober Team, the studio responsible for Layers of Fear, Observer, and the recent Blair Witch adaptation. But it may not release in Australia: a ruling on the Classification Board website (first spotted by Kotaku) indicates it has been refused classification. 'Refused classification' means the game is effectively banned in Australia, due to breaking some (yet to be specified) rule. Most recently, it emerged that Wasteland 3 was almost banned in Australia for breaking a clause related to a supposedly indecent depiction of drug use.  As for why The Medium has been refused classification: we don't know. I've reached out to the board for the reason, but since it was rated by the IARC (International Age Rating Coalition) rather than the board itself, the issue could be as simple as a data entry error. IARC submissions are done via questionnaire "programmed with unique algorithms that assign ratings for each of the participating rating authorities which reflect their own distinct local standards about the age appropriateness of various content featured in the app." Also, it's not uncommon for a refused classification ruling to come good. Some studios modify their games to conform to the laws, whether globally or regionally. Whatever the case, you can still pre-order The Medium on Steam at the time of writing. The game is scheduled to release on December 10. I've reached out to the Classification Board for the reason behind the decision, and will update this story when I hear back.

notes.title: Reunited for The Medium

Bloober Team Reunites Top Talent Featuring Troy Baker, Mary Elizabeth McGlynn, and Akira Yamaoka for Collaboration on The Medium

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37714620/9d9212fb1fbf5b1e43df65aeb9283051f4ea80d4.png[/img]

Troy Baker will voice The Maw, the main spirit world entity and antagonist in The Medium. Mary Elizabeth McGlynn, having worked together with legendary game composer Akira Yamaoka on the Silent Hill series, will be providing her vocals for the original soundtrack. 

The three will be bringing their unique talent and passion from their previous work together to our largest and most ambitious project to date.

notes.title: BLOOBER TEAM ANNOUNCES PSYCHOLOGICAL HORROR GAME, THE MEDIUM
notes.notes:
Bloober Team, the makers of Blair Witch, Observer and Layers of Fear, today announces its largest and most ambitious project to date - The Medium. 

The Medium is a tension-fuelled, psychological horror game built around a central motif: how your perspective changes your perception. 

https://youtu.be/tTAz758Vt88 

Players will find themselves in the body of Marianne, a medium hounded by visions, living and interacting across two worlds: the real, and the spirit world. Nothing is what it seems, everything has another side. As a medium with access to both worlds, you have a wider perspective and can see more clearly that there’s no one simple truth to what others perceive.  

“Every one of our games has a central theme that drives its creative and technological design. In The Medium, we focus on perspective and perception. When you change your point of view, you discover that things are more complicated and nuanced than you initially thought" - said Piotr Babieno, CEO at Bloober Team. "The Medium is our most ambitious game ever and we can't wait to show you how we're translating this vision into a psychological horror.”

The legendary composer Akira Yamaoka and Bloober Team’s Arkadiusz Reikowski are working together on the game’s original ‘dual’ score, creating truly unique atmospheres across both worlds.
